facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells that were uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, which is a characteristic feature of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient has a history of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts, which are characteristic features of myelodysplastic syndrome.

The patient's bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts, and next-generation sequencing revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes, which are characteristic features of acute myeloid leukemia.
The patient's skin biopsy showed a BRAF-V600E variant status, which is a characteristic feature of certain tumors.
The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, which could be consistent with cutaneous lymphoma.

rationales.F05: Monocytoid-appearing cells in skin biopsy suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rationales.F06: CD207/langerin positivity is characteristic of Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rationales.F08: BRAF-V600E variant status is often associated with BRAF-V600E positive tumors
